analysis.title: Global Equity Compass - November 2026: A more discerning market
key_insights: October saw investors scrutinise assumptions behind the year's strongest performers, particularly AI. Markets are questioning whether current AI investment can turn into future earnings, not AI's potential.
AllianzGI strongly believes markets are being impatient on AI, as pricing a payoff years away requires staying the course.
Areas outside tech are attracting more attention while some AI beneficiaries are under pressure. Headline index moves conceal wide differences.
Elevated government-bond yields raise the return required from equities. Companies need stronger earnings growth, reliable cash generation and disciplined capital use, which could widen dispersion.
The AI theme is shifting from spending on chips, data centres and compute to who can convert adoption into productivity gains and profits. This could broaden opportunities to AI users.

Europe's drive for autonomy is moving from commitment to implementation across defence, energy, semiconductors and industrial capacity. Beneficiaries may extend to suppliers, tech providers and industrials.
Style lens: Momentum reversed sharply in October after September's rebound, and Quality also lost ground after holding up for much of the year.
Value was the clear October beneficiary, reversing September's weakness, as participation broadened beyond expensive growth.
Chart of the month: in four of five hiking cycles, markets underpriced Fed tightening, with an average shortfall of 109bp. Priced-in rate paths should not be treated as a ceiling.
If rates rise more than expected, repricing hits long-duration and richly valued stocks, so balance sheet strength, pricing power and earnings resilience matter more.
Market data as of 30 Oct 2026: MSCI World Value +19.97% over 12M versus Growth +2.71%. CSI 300 -12.40% over 3M and Nifty 50 -5.20% over 3M, CAC 40 -6.08% over 3M.

sector_views.rationale: Value led the October rotation as investors embraced cheaper and more cyclical areas.
European autonomy spending may show up in order books and earnings, including among suppliers and enablers.
Long-term AI payoff is supported, but the market is shifting to earnings delivery and capital discipline.

earnings_insights: The report argues companies must show stronger earnings growth and reliable cash generation to justify stretched valuations given elevated yields.
AI capex is expected to need conversion into profits. European autonomy investment could become visible in order books and earnings.

macro_indicators.indicator: Fed rate hike underpricing, average of five cycles
macro_indicators.interpretation: Markets have historically underpriced Fed tightening, so the current priced path may not be a ceiling and long-duration equities are at risk.
Raises the hurdle return required from equities.

risk_factors: Fed tightening being underpriced could cause faster discount-rate repricing hitting long-duration stocks.
Stretched valuations amid elevated bond yields.
AI investment failing to convert to earnings.
charts_described: Chart of the month shows over- or underpricing of Fed hikes on a 12m horizon in bp: 1994-95 -165, 1999-2000 -78, 2004-06 -16, 2015-18 +8, 2022-23 -296, average -109.
vol_and_positioning: Momentum fell sharply in October after September's rebound, and Quality lost ground, indicating rotation out of crowded winners.
Value outperformed in October as market participation broadened.
geopolitical: Ongoing geopolitical uncertainty is cited as part of the environment rewarding selectivity.
Europe's drive for strategic autonomy in defence, energy, semiconductors and industrial capacity.

tension_points.bear_case: Investors are scrutinising whether today's exceptional investment can translate into earnings, and some AI beneficiaries are under pressure.
